country.comment: Explicitly stated in the article title, author affiliations, abstract (Shillong city), and Section 1 (India).
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Title and Abstract; PDF p. 2, Section 1 (Introduction)

effect_estimate.comment: Cached PDF is a 2-page publisher preview (journal pp. 251–252 of 251–277) that cuts off mid-sentence in Section 1 before the Methods and Results sections. Only the Abstract's headline qualitative summary is accessible; no quantitative estimates from pp. 253–277 are available in the provided text.
effect_estimate.value: Abstract headline finding only (partial 2-page PDF preview, pp. 251–252 of 251–277; no numeric effect estimate reported in accessible pages): in non-municipal areas of Shillong, domestic water inequity is more prominent and widespread, local institutions (dorbar shnong) play a greater and more significant role in water governance, and water distribution and governance by local institutions are complementary.

mechanism_certainty.comment: Cached PDF contains only pages 251–252 of 251–277 (Abstract and start of Section 1), omitting the Methods and Results sections (pp. 253–277); therefore it cannot be determined whether the empirical analysis directly observes the administrative/institutional mechanism (2), documents an association (1), or infers it (0).
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF pp. 1–2 (journal pp. 251–252 of 251–277; truncated in Section 1)

mechanism_flags.comment: Abstract, Keywords, and Section 1 explicitly identify the division of Shillong localities between formal municipal areas and informal non-municipal areas (service_area under ELIGIBILITY) and the multi-institution governance split/complementarity between formal municipal authorities and informal local traditional institutions, the dorbar shnong (institutional_fragmentation under DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION). Pages 253–277 are absent from the cached preview.
mechanism_flags.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract and Keywords; PDF p. 2, Section 1 (Introduction)

outcome_flags.comment: Abstract explicitly states that the study examines domestic urban water supply systems using four indicators—quantity, quality, accessibility, and reliability—and Section 1 reiterates domestic water distribution and accessibility.
outcome_flags.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF p. 2, Section 1 (Introduction)

publication_year.comment: Explicitly printed in copyright line and journal citation header on both pages.
publication_year.where_found: PDF p. 1, journal header and copyright line; PDF p. 2, running header

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: Cached PDF is a 2-page Brill preview (pp. 251–252 of 251–277) ending mid-sentence in Section 1 before the Methods section; cannot determine whether the empirical design in pp. 253–277 is primary qualitative (CASP), quantitative cross-sectional survey (JBI), or mixed-methods (MMAT).
risk_of_bias_tool.where_found: PDF pp. 1–2 (journal pp. 251–252 of 251–277; Methods section missing)

sample_size.comment: Not reported in the accessible 2-page PDF preview (journal pp. 251–252 of 251–277); text cuts off mid-sentence at the end of PDF p. 2 in Section 1 (‘selected localities (non-municipal) of’) prior to the Methods section.
sample_size.where_found: PDF pp. 1–2 (journal pp. 251–252 of 251–277; truncated in Section 1)

study_design.comment: Specific empirical design (e.g., qualitative interviews, household survey, or mixed methods) is not reported in the accessible 2-page preview (journal pp. 251–252 of 251–277), which describes examining water supply indicators (quantity, quality, accessibility, reliability) and local governance in selected non-municipal localities of Shillong before cutting off in Section 1.
study_design.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF p. 2, Section 1 (truncated at p. 252 of 251–277)
